raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### What does this PR do?

Optimal token baseline (`optimal_token_baseline`, `tir_optimal_token_baseline`) does not work on the V1 trainer, which `main_ppo` now uses by default. Step 1 fails with:

```
AssertionError: Step-dependent optimal baseline requires sum_pi_squared from actor. Please set actor.calculate_sum_pi_squared=True in config.
```

This happens even when `actor.calculate_sum_pi_squared=True` is set. #6153 wired `sum_pi_squared` into the engine and the legacy `ray_trainer.py`, but V1's `PPOTrainer` does not pass it through:

- `_compute_old_log_prob` never puts `calculate_sum_pi_squared` into `extra_info`, so the engine never computes it.
- It also never reads `sum_pi_squared` back from TransferQueue.
- `_compute_advantage` does not select it, so `compute_advantage()` never sees it.

The fix forwards the flag. When the flag is set, it reads the actor's `sum_pi_squared`, slices it to the response with `response_from_nested`, and writes it back. This is the same left shift used for `old_log_probs` and `entropy`. `_compute_advantage` then fetches it. With the flag off, nothing changes.

**Not a duplicate:**
- Searched open and closed PRs and issues for `sum_pi_squared`, `optimal token baseline` and `optimal_token_baseline v1`. #6153 and #5615 (both merged) only cover the legacy trainer. #7473 (open) touches `ray_trainer.py` only, and #8026 (open) leaves `sum_pi_squared` alone.
- Query: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=sum_pi_squared

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=sum_pi_squared
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

**CPU unit test:** `tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_sum_pi_squared_on_cpu.py` uses an in-memory TransferQueue stand-in. It checks three things:
- the flag reaches `extra_info`;
- the stored `sum_pi_squared` is the response-aligned slice (and is left untouched when the flag is off);
- OTB and TIR-OTB produce finite advantages through `_compute_advantage`.

```
pytest -q tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_sum_pi_squared_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_trainer_base_on_cpu.py
# with this PR: 14 passed
# test_sum_pi_squared_on_cpu.py on main: 4 failed (KeyError: 'calculate_sum_pi_squared' x2, OTB AssertionError x2)
```

**GPU run:** 1x RTX 4090, main @ 3c6d9b4, V1 sync trainer, Qwen3-0.6B, GSM8K, batch 32 × n=4, 3 steps, vLLM rollout, `actor.calculate_sum_pi_squared=True`, `rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4`:

| run | result | `rollout_probs_diff_mean` | `critic/advantages/mean` | `critic/advantages/max` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, `optimal_token_baseline` | AssertionError at step 1 | – | – | – |
| this PR, `optimal_token_baseline` | 3/3 steps | 0.0058 / 0.0059 / 0.0056 | 0.0062 / 0.0030 / -0.0002 | 1.28 / 1.38 / 1.16 |
| this PR, `tir_optimal_token_baseline` | 3/3 steps | 0.0058 / 0.0059 / 0.0056 | 0.0086 / 0.0008 / -0.0019 | 1.50 / 1.00 / 0.99 |

Side note, not changed here: with the default `log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=16`, step 2 OOMs on a 24 GB card in `calculate_sum_pi_squared_from_logits`. The cause is `logsumexp(2.0 * logits)`, which materializes another full-vocabulary copy, about 5 GB for a packed micro-batch. A chunked version like `entropy_from_logits_with_chunking` would avoid this; I can follow up if that is wanted.

### Design & Code Changes

`verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`:
- `_compute_old_log_prob`:
  - add `calculate_sum_pi_squared` to `extra_info`;
  - when it is set, select `sum_pi_squared`, slice it to the response, and write it to TransferQueue next to `old_log_probs` / `entropy`.
- `_compute_advantage`: select `sum_pi_squared` when the flag is set.

- [ ] Apply [pre-commit checks](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-linting-and-formatting): `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files --show-diff-on-failure --color=always`
- [ ] Add / Update [the documentation](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/docs).
- [x] Add unit or end-to-end test(s) to [the CI workflow](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/tree/main/.github/workflows) to cover all the code. If not feasible, explain why: `tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_sum_pi_squared_on_cpu.py` is picked up by the CPU unit test workflow.
- [ ] Once your PR is ready for CI, send a message in [the `ci-request` channel](https://verl-project.slack.com/archives/C091TCESWB1) in [the `verl` Slack workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/verl-project/shared_invite/zt-3855yhg8g-CTkqXu~hKojPCmo7k_yXTQ). **AI assistance:** This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude), which helped locate the bug through GPU config sweeps, write the fix and tests, and run the commands above.

detail.body:
### What does this PR do?

Optimal token baseline (`optimal_token_baseline`, `tir_optimal_token_baseline`) does not work on the V1 trainer, which `main_ppo` now uses by default. Step 1 fails with:

```
AssertionError: Step-dependent optimal baseline requires sum_pi_squared from actor. Please set actor.calculate_sum_pi_squared=True in config.
```

This happens even when `actor.calculate_sum_pi_squared=True` is set. #6153 wired `sum_pi_squared` into the engine and the legacy `ray_trainer.py`, but V1's `PPOTrainer` does not pass it through:

- `_compute_old_log_prob` never puts `calculate_sum_pi_squared` into `extra_info`, so the engine never computes it.
- It also never reads `sum_pi_squared` back from TransferQueue.
- `_compute_advantage` does not select it, so `compute_advantage()` never sees it.

The fix forwards the flag. When the flag is set, it reads the actor's `sum_pi_squared`, slices it to the response with `response_from_nested`, and writes it back. This is the same left shift used for `old_log_probs` and `entropy`. `_compute_advantage` then fetches it. With the flag off, nothing changes.

**Not a duplicate:**
- Searched open and closed PRs and issues for `sum_pi_squared`, `optimal token baseline` and `optimal_token_baseline v1`. #6153 and #5615 (both merged) only cover the legacy trainer. #7473 (open) touches `ray_trainer.py` only, and #8026 (open) leaves `sum_pi_squared` alone.
- Query: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=sum_pi_squared

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Search for similar PRs. Paste at least one query link here: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=sum_pi_squared
- [x] Format the PR title as `[{modules}] {type}: {description}` (This will be checked by the CI)

### Test

**CPU unit test:** `tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_sum_pi_squared_on_cpu.py` uses an in-memory TransferQueue stand-in. It checks three things:
- the flag reaches `extra_info`;
- the stored `sum_pi_squared` is the response-aligned slice (and is left untouched when the flag is off);
- OTB and TIR-OTB produce finite advantages through `_compute_advantage`.

```
pytest -q tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_sum_pi_squared_on_cpu.py tests/trainer/ppo/v1/test_trainer_base_on_cpu.py
# with this PR: 14 passed
# test_sum_pi_squared_on_cpu.py on main: 4 failed (KeyError: 'calculate_sum_pi_squared' x2, OTB AssertionError x2)
```

**GPU run:** 1x RTX 4090, main @ 3c6d9b4, V1 sync trainer, Qwen3-0.6B, GSM8K, batch 32 × n=4, 3 steps, vLLM rollout, `actor.calculate_sum_pi_squared=True`, `rollout.log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=4`:

| run | result | `rollout_probs_diff_mean` | `critic/advantages/mean` | `critic/advantages/max` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, `optimal_token_baseline` | AssertionError at step 1 | – | – | – |
| this PR, `optimal_token_baseline` | 3/3 steps | 0.0058 / 0.0059 / 0.0056 | 0.0062 / 0.0030 / -0.0002 | 1.28 / 1.38 / 1.16 |
| this PR, `tir_optimal_token_baseline` | 3/3 steps | 0.0058 / 0.0059 / 0.0056 | 0.0086 / 0.0008 / -0.0019 | 1.50 / 1.00 / 0.99 |

Side note, not changed here: with the default `log_prob_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=16`, step 2 OOMs on a 24 GB card in `calculate_sum_pi_squared_from_logits`. The cause is `logsumexp(2.0 * logits)`, which materializes another full-vocabulary copy, about 5 GB for a packed micro-batch. A chunked version like `entropy_from_logits_with_chunking` would avoid this; I can follow up if that is wanted.

`verl/trainer/ppo/v1/trainer_base.py`:
- `_compute_old_log_prob`:
  - add `calculate_sum_pi_squared` to `extra_info`;
  - when it is set, select `sum_pi_squared`, slice it to the response, and write it to TransferQueue next to `old_log_probs` / `entropy`.
- `_compute_advantage`: select `sum_pi_squared` when the flag is set.

+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock

+import pytest
+import torch

+from tensordict import TensorDict
+
+import verl.trainer.ppo.v1.trainer_base as trainer_base
+from verl.trainer.ppo.v1.trainer_base import PPOTrainer
+
+PROMPT_LENS = [3, 2]
+RESPONSE_LENS = [4, 2]
+
+
+class _StubTrainer(PPOTrainer):
+    def on_step_end(self):
+        pass
+
+    def on_sample_end(self):
+        pass
+
+
+class _FakeTQ:
+    """In-memory stand-in for the TransferQueue key-value API used by the trainer."""
+
+    def __init__(self, fields: dict):
+        self.store = dict(fields)
+
+    def kv_batch_get(self, keys, partition_id, select_fields):
+        return TensorDict({k: self.store[k] for k in select_fields if k in self.store}, batch_size=len(keys))
+
+    def kv_batch_put(self, keys, partition_id, fields):
+        for k in fields.keys():
+            self.store[k] = fields[k]
+        return SimpleNamespace(keys=keys, partition_id=partition_id, extra_info={})
+
+
+class _Batch(SimpleNamespace):
+    def __len__(self):
+        return len(self.keys)
+
+
+def _nested(rows):
+    return torch.nested.as_nested_tensor(rows, layout=torch.jagged)
+
+
+def _make_trainer(calculate_sum_pi_squared: bool, adv_estimator: str = "optimal_token_baseline"):
+    trainer = _StubTrainer.__new__(_StubTrainer)
+    trainer.config = OmegaConf.create(
+        {
+            "algorithm": {
+                "adv_estimator": adv_estimator,
+                "gamma": 1.0,
+                "lam": 1.0,
+                "use_kl_in_reward": False,
+                "norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo": True,
+                "rollout_correction": None,
+            },
+            "actor_rollout_ref": {
+                "actor": {
+                    "calculate_sum_pi_squared": calculate_sum_pi_squared,
+                    "loss_agg_mode": "token-mean",
+                    "loss_scale_factor": None,
+                },
+                "rollout": {"n": 2, "temperature": 1.0, "calculate_log_probs": False},
+            },
+        }
+    )
+    trainer.actor_rollout_wg = MagicMock()
+    trainer.actor_rollout_wg.compute_log_prob.side_effect = lambda batch: list(batch.keys)
+    return trainer
+
+
+def _fake_tq_with_actor_outputs():
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    seq_lens = [p + r for p, r in zip(PROMPT_LENS, RESPONSE_LENS, strict=True)]
+    # The actor writes per-position outputs over the whole sequence; position t predicts token t + 1.
+    full = {name: _nested([torch.rand(n) for n in seq_lens]) for name in ("log_probs", "entropy", "sum_pi_squared")}
+    return _FakeTQ(
+        {
+            **full,
+            "response_mask": _nested([torch.ones(r, dtype=torch.long) for r in RESPONSE_LENS]),
+            "rm_scores": _nested([torch.tensor([0.0] * (r - 1) + [float(i)]) for i, r in enumerate(RESPONSE_LENS)]),
+            "uid": torch.tensor([0, 0]),
+        }
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("calculate_sum_pi_squared", [True, False])
+def test_old_log_prob_writes_response_aligned_sum_pi_squared(monkeypatch, calculate_sum_pi_squared):
+    fake_tq = _fake_tq_with_actor_outputs()
+    full_sum_pi_squared = fake_tq.store["sum_pi_squared"]
+    monkeypatch.setattr(trainer_base, "tq", fake_tq)
+    trainer = _make_trainer(calculate_sum_pi_squared)
+    batch = _Batch(keys=["a", "b"], partition_id="train", extra_info={})
+
+    trainer._compute_old_log_prob(batch, metrics={})
+
+    assert batch.extra_info["calculate_sum_pi_squared"] is calculate_sum_pi_squared
+    stored = fake_tq.store["sum_pi_squared"]
+    if not calculate_sum_pi_squared:
+        assert stored is full_sum_pi_squared
+        return
+    for row, full_row, prompt_len, response_len in zip(
+        stored.unbind(), full_sum_pi_squared.unbind(), PROMPT_LENS, RESPONSE_LENS, strict=True
+    ):
+        # Same left shift as old_log_probs: the response tokens are predicted from positions [P-1, P+R-1).
+        torch.testing.assert_close(row, full_row[prompt_len - 1 : prompt_len + response_len - 1])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("adv_estimator", ["optimal_token_baseline", "tir_optimal_token_baseline"])
+def test_optimal_token_baseline_receives_sum_pi_squared(monkeypatch, adv_estimator):
+    fake_tq = _fake_tq_with_actor_outputs()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(trainer_base, "tq", fake_tq)
+    trainer = _make_trainer(calculate_sum_pi_squared=True, adv_estimator=adv_estimator)
+    batch = _Batch(keys=["a", "b"], partition_id="train", extra_info={})
+
+    trainer._compute_old_log_prob(batch, metrics={})
+    trainer._compute_advantage(batch, metrics={})
+
+    advantages = fake_tq.store["advantages"]
+    assert [len(row) for row in advantages.unbind()] == RESPONSE_LENS
+    assert all(torch.isfinite(row).all() for row in advantages.unbind())
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("ref_in_actor", [True, False])
+def test_ref_log_prob_keeps_actor_sum_pi_squared(monkeypatch, ref_in_actor):
+    fake_tq = _fake_tq_with_actor_outputs()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(trainer_base, "tq", fake_tq)
+    trainer = _make_trainer(calculate_sum_pi_squared=True)
+    trainer.ref_in_actor = ref_in_actor
+    trainer.ref_policy_wg = MagicMock()
+    trainer.ref_policy_wg.compute_ref_log_prob.side_effect = lambda batch: list(batch.keys)
+    batch = _Batch(keys=["a", "b"], partition_id="train", extra_info={})
+
+    trainer._compute_old_log_prob(batch, metrics={})
+    trainer._compute_ref_log_prob(batch, metrics={})
+
+    # The reference pass must not compute (and so overwrite) sum_pi_squared.
+    assert batch.extra_info["calculate_sum_pi_squared"] is False
+
+
+def test_bypass_mode_rejects_sum_pi_squared(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(trainer_base, "tq", _fake_tq_with_actor_outputs())
+    trainer = _make_trainer(calculate_sum_pi_squared=True)
+    trainer.config.algorithm.rollout_correction = {"bypass_mode": True}
+    batch = _Batch(keys=["a", "b"], partition_id="train", extra_info={})
+
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="bypass_mode"):
+        trainer._compute_old_log_prob(batch, metrics={})
